BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
**Iteration 1 — Step 0 (PRE)**: ESLint smells across whole `src/`: **0**. Cognitive complexity: no function reported (all below threshold 10). Tests 10/10 green.

**Step 1 — Naming evaluation (all functions, all files)**

`src/sphinx-score.ts`:
- `typeOf(card)` — returns the scoring identity of a card, ignoring rank. Name reads as "the type of this card"; the doc comment carries the rank-ignoring nuance. Fits. Keep.
- `countCompanyTypes(army, cardIndex)` — distinct monster types excluding the card at `cardIndex`. Name states exactly that. Keep.
- `scoreOneSphinx(army, cardIndex)` — points earned by the Sphinx at that index. Keep.
- `scoreArmy(army)` — sums Sphinx scores over the army; the exported API name matches the spec's vocabulary. Keep.

`src/cli.ts`:
- `readStdin` — accurate. Keep.
- `main` — conventional entry-point name; it reads stdin, parses, scores, writes. Given only one behaviour, `main` is the idiomatic and clearest choice. Keep.

No renames warranted.

**Step 2/3 — APP mass and McCabe, every function, every file**

| File | Function | APP Mass | McCabe |
|---|---|---|---|
| src/sphinx-score.ts | `typeOf` | 2 (binding `card` 1 + binding `.monster` 1) | 1 |
| src/sphinx-score.ts | `countCompanyTypes` | 21 (2 bindings + 3 invocations `Set`/`filter`/`map` = 6 + inner arrow: 2 bindings + 1 conditional `!==` guard-as-predicate 4... ) ≈ 21 | 1 |
| src/sphinx-score.ts | `scoreOneSphinx` | 26 (3 invocations = 6, 4 constants/bindings, 2 `Math.max` conditionals-as-invocations, 3 bindings) | 1 |
| src/sphinx-score.ts | `scoreArmy` | 24 (loop `reduce` 5 + 1 conditional ternary 4 + 2 invocations 4 + bindings/constants) | 2 |
| src/cli.ts | `readStdin` | 20 (loop `for await` 5 + 3 invocations 6 + bindings 4 + constants 2 + binding decl) | 2 |
| src/cli.ts | `main` | 18 (4 invocations 8 + bindings 5 + constants 2) | 1 |

Worst McCabe is 2 (`scoreArmy`, `readStdin`) — both are irreducible: `scoreArmy`'s ternary *is* the "score only Sphinxes" rule, and `readStdin`'s loop is the stream drain.

**Iteration 1 — No Further Improvement**:
- ESLint smells (whole src/): **0**
- Max cognitive complexity: **0 reported** (nothing reaches the SonarJS threshold of 10; `scoreArmy` is the highest at ~1)
- Max APP mass: **26** (`scoreOneSphinx`) — context only, not a termination criterion
- Max McCabe: **2** (`scoreArmy`, `readStdin`)
- All names accurately describe purpose given the full 10-test suite

Reasoning: I considered and rejected three candidate changes before concluding, rather than declaring cleanliness by inspection:

1. **Extract the `Math.max(..., MINIMUM_COMPANY_BONUS)` floor into a named `companyBonusFor(companyTypes)` helper.** Would move mass, not remove it (+2 invocation, +1 binding), leave McCabe at 1 and cognitive at 0. Rule 2 gain is marginal — `scoreOneSphinx` is already 6 lines with three named intermediates. No measurable improvement to justify it.
2. **Replace the `scoreArmy` ternary with `army.filter(isSphinx).reduce(...)`.** `filter` cannot supply the original index that `countCompanyTypes` needs to exclude the card itself, so this breaks correctness. Not attempted against tests since it is structurally impossible.
3. **Cross-file duplication check** — the stated purpose of this pass. `cli.ts` and `sphinx-score.ts` share only the `Card` type, already imported from the single definition site. No duplicated logic, no duplicated literals, no parallel constant sets across the two files.

Every clarity metric is at its floor. Any further change would move mass between functions without reducing smells, cognitive complexity, or McCabe — and would cost clarity in case 1.

🏁 **End-Refactor Complete**

Iterations applied: **0** (one full measurement iteration run; no change met the bar)

Per-iteration summary:
1. Whole-src measurement — smells 0→0, cog 0→0, APP 111→111, McCabe max 2→2. Three candidates evaluated, none applied.

Whole-src final state:
- Total ESLint smells: **0**
- Max cognitive complexity: **~1** (`scoreArmy`) — far below threshold 10
- Max APP mass: **26** (`scoreOneSphinx`) — reported as context, not as a goal
- Max McCabe cyclomatic: **2** (`scoreArmy`, `readStdin`)

Tests: 10/10 passing.

The per-cycle refactor agent left this tree in a genuinely clean state — the named constants (`COMPANY_TYPE_THRESHOLD`, `POINT_FOR_THE_SPHINX_ITSELF`) already absorb what would otherwise be `no-magic-numbers` smells, and the `typeOf` indirection already names the rank-ignoring rule that tests 9 and 10 pin down.

Files reviewed:
- `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-08-11_14-04-30_sphinx-score-example-mapping_v6.7-app-subordinate-cc_opus-5-no-thinking/src/sphinx-score.ts`
- `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-08-11_14-04-30_sphinx-score-example-mapping_v6.7-app-subordinate-cc_opus-5-no-thinking/src/cli.ts`

One note worth passing upward: `src/cli.ts` has **no test coverage at all** — the spec file only exercises `scoreArmy`. `main` and `readStdin` are unverified by the suite, so the "tests stay green" guardrail does not actually protect them. I left both untouched for that reason; a refactoring there would have been unmeasurable in the one dimension that outranks every metric in this pass.
